name: ADMX
notes: The commonly reported history that ADMX was built at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in 1995 and moved to CENPA in 2010 has no checkable primary citation, so it is not recorded as a dated interval.
No numeric magnet field strength or cavity volume was found with a clean verbatim quote in the sources consulted, so neither is listed in key_specs.

physics_goals.quote: ADMX is an axion haloscope, which uses a strong magnetic field to convert dark matter axions to detectable to microwave photons.
physics_goals.value: Detect or exclude QCD axion dark matter via resonant conversion to microwave photons in a strong magnetic field

summary.plain: ADMX searches for the axion, a hypothetical particle that could make up dark matter. At the University of Washington, a tunable metal cavity sits inside a powerful magnet, hunting for a faint microwave signal that dark-matter axions would produce.
summary.technical: Cavity haloscope search for galactic-halo dark-matter axions using a tunable, dilution-refrigerator-cooled (90 mK) copper-plated resonant cavity inside a superconducting solenoid, sited at CENPA (University of Washington) and managed by Fermilab; successive Gen 2 runs have scanned KSVZ- and DFSZ-sensitive parameter space from roughly 1-3.7 GHz equivalent axion mass, most recently 1.10-1.31 GHz (2025).

unique_capabilities.quote: ADMX set a new record as the first ever axion experiment to reach the DFSZ sensitivity with its new results from 2017
unique_capabilities.value: First axion haloscope to reach DFSZ-model sensitivity, in its 2017 result
